# Verify PixyPup for real

"The code looks right" is not verification. Run it, drive it, look at what it actually does,
and attach the evidence.

## Setup (in the worktree you were given; never the main tree if another agent is working there)

1. Fresh worktree: `git worktree add --detach <scratch>/verify-<n> <ref>`, then `cd` there and `npm ci`.
2. If `node_modules/electron/dist` is missing (the postinstall download was skipped), run `node node_modules/electron/install.js` once.
3. Only if the change touches `native/`: `bash scripts/build-native.sh` and run `native/bin/pixyhelper windows` (prints JSON).
4. API-bound checks (SAM, Muse Image, Spark, voice) need `MODEL_API_KEY` in the environment. Never write the key anywhere. If it's absent, run the offline checks and report the API checks as `GO-WITH-GAP: no key`.

## Start it

- Free the ports first: `lsof -ti tcp:9222 -ti tcp:5173` must print nothing; if it does, it's another checkout: stop and report, don't kill it.
- Start (Bash with `run_in_background`): `npx electron-vite dev --remoteDebuggingPort 9222 > <scratch>/dev.log 2>&1`
- If the maintainer may be running the app, or the check needs no Meta call: `env -u MODEL_API_KEY npx electron-vite dev --remoteDebuggingPort 9333 -- --user-data-dir=<scratch>/userdata` with a `settings.json` of `{"onboarded": true}` already in that dir. Otherwise first-launch onboarding opens on the maintainer's screen, and a pet made there runs the real pipeline on the key (2026-11-01 husky). Check that 5173, 5174 and 9333 are free first.
- Ready when `curl -s http://127.0.0.1:9222/json` lists a page whose `url` contains `/overlay/index.html` (poll up to ~20 s), and `<scratch>/dev.log` shows `starting electron app` with no `Error`.
- This checkout: `lsof -ti tcp:5173 | head -1 | xargs -I{} lsof -a -p {} -d cwd -Fn` prints this worktree's path.

Before trusting any result, confirm the process you're talking to is THIS checkout (an old
server on the same port from another worktree is the classic false result). Never point anything
at production.

## Drive it

Drive the renderer over CDP with Node 22's built-in WebSocket. Save this once as `<scratch>/cdp.mjs`:

```js
// usage: node cdp.mjs <page-url-substring> <method> '<json params>'
const [match, method, params = '{}'] = process.argv.slice(2);
const pages = await (await fetch('http://127.0.0.1:9222/json')).json();
const page = pages.find((p) => p.url.includes(match));
if (!page) { console.error('no page matching', match, pages.map((p) => p.url)); process.exit(1); }
const ws = new WebSocket(page.webSocketDebuggerUrl);
await new Promise((r) => (ws.onopen = r));
ws.onmessage = (e) => { const m = JSON.parse(e.data); if (m.id === 1) { console.log(JSON.stringify(m.result ?? m.error)); ws.close(); } };
ws.send(JSON.stringify({ id: 1, method, params: JSON.parse(params) }));
```

Core journeys:
- **J2 pet on screen (overlay):** wait ~1 s after the page is listed (the first read right after load returns `""` because no animation frame has run yet; verified 2026-10-31). Then `node <scratch>/cdp.mjs /overlay/ Runtime.evaluate '{"expression":"document.getElementById(\"pup\").style.transform","returnByValue":true}'` twice, 1 s apart: the translate x must change (walking). Drag: dispatch `Input.dispatchMouseEvent` mousePressed/mouseMoved/mouseReleased on the pup's centre and re-read the transform.
- **Click-through:** CDP sees only the renderer. To prove clicks pass through to the desktop, the brief must allow a computer-use session (screenshot + click an app behind the overlay); otherwise report it as a gap, never as passed.
- **J1 photo → pet:** `npm run pose-test -- assets/photos/<file>` (needs the key; costs well under $0.10) writes `out/pose-test/` + `report.md`; once onboarding exists, drive its page (`/onboarding/`) the same way.
- **J3 screen reactions:** pure decisions are covered by `ruleDecide` tests; live: open a Terminal running a failing `npx vitest run` on a fixture test, a window named Zoom, then read the overlay's state over CDP.
- **J4 voice:** `matchCommand` tests offline; live needs the mic permission and the key: say the pet's name + "sit", read the overlay state.

Use `.claude/ceo/feature-map.md` (if present) to go straight to a feature. If an entry is wrong,
report the correction as a `FACT:` line.

## Inspect it (runtime eyes)

- Main-process stdout/stderr: `<scratch>/dev.log`.
- Renderer console: CDP `Runtime.enable` then read `Runtime.consoleAPICalled` events (extend `cdp.mjs` to keep the socket open for N seconds), or `Runtime.evaluate` any DOM/state expression.
- Screenshot of the overlay page (works without the macOS Screen Recording permission): `node <scratch>/cdp.mjs /overlay/ Page.captureScreenshot '{}'` → base64 `data` → `<scratch>/overlay.png`. It shows the transparent overlay only, not the desktop behind it.
- Performance: CDP `Performance.enable` + `Performance.getMetrics` (JSHeapUsedSize, TaskDuration) sampled twice 10 s apart; a walking pet must not grow the heap.
- Main process debugging: add `--inspect 9229` to the dev command and attach.
- NOT available: `screencapture` of the real desktop (Screen Recording permission not granted to the agent's terminal); real OS click-through checks without computer use.

- Animation changes: green gates say nothing about looks. Collect the distinct `#pup` srcs while `__pixyDebug.state === 'walk'`, composite 8 into a strip PNG in the page (canvas.toDataURL) and look at it; for motion, record ~120 frames of the pup (src + computed transform) at 30 fps and `ffmpeg` them into a GIF. `__pixyDebug.rig` exposes the dog/cat walk rig (kind, bellyY, centroids).
- Real J1 runs from an isolated profile: the key is exported in the maintainer's login shell, so launch through `zsh -lic "PIXY_DEV_PHOTO=<photo> npx electron-vite dev --remoteDebuggingPort 9333 -- --user-data-dir=<scratch>/ud"` (no settings.json → onboarding), then on `/onboarding/` evaluate `await __ob.devPhoto(); await pixyOb.createPet('<name>','<species>')`. The pack lands in `<scratch>/ud/pets/<name>`; load it later with `PIXY_PACK_DIR`. Only with the maintainer's go-ahead to spend credits (2026-11-01: yes).

A performance claim needs a measurement (a trace, a profile, timings over N runs), not a code read.
A memory claim needs a snapshot diff. A visual claim needs a screenshot at every required viewport.

## Evidence to attach

Gate output tails; each CDP command and its JSON result; `<scratch>/overlay.png` path for any visual claim; `dev.log` tail (last 30 lines, every error line in full); for API checks the request count and wall time (never the key or image bytes); `out/pose-test/report.md` for pose runs.

## Teardown

Kill the background dev process you started (its PID, then `lsof -ti tcp:9222 -ti tcp:5173` must be empty), remove `<scratch>/cdp.mjs` outputs you no longer need, `git worktree remove <scratch>/verify-<n>`.
